metadata.database: A Deeper China | Beijing decision layer

BJM01.guest_need: A first-time visitor wants imperial Beijing to become meaningful rather than overwhelming.
BJM01.hidden_need: Reduce cognitive and queue load by choosing one bounded reading question.
BJM01.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One imperial-axis reading plus one contrast explains order and scale better than collecting every hall.
BJM01.stop_condition: The guest can explain one spatial or political idea after the bounded Palace Museum visit.
BJM01.low_energy_branch: Keep one confirmed palace sequence and one short elevation reset.
BJM01.rain_branch: Protect the confirmed indoor core and remove exposed park movement.
BJM01.body_cost: Moderate walking, high attention load, screening, queues and weather exposure.

BJM02.guest_need: A visitor wants Beijing beyond palace architecture through ritual, park and commerce.
BJM02.hidden_need: Create a public-life contrast without adding another monument.
BJM02.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One ritual/park anchor and one south-of-axis transition answer public-life change better than another imperial site.
BJM02.stop_condition: The guest can distinguish ritual space, park use and commercial street life.
BJM02.low_energy_branch: Choose one park/ritual anchor and protect a seated pause.
BJM02.rain_branch: Keep the covered interpretation and remove the long open-park segment.
BJM02.body_cost: Low-to-moderate walking but large open areas and heat can accumulate.

BJM03.guest_need: A visitor wants hutongs as neighbourhoods, not as a staged tourist set.
BJM03.hidden_need: Balance visual interest with resident privacy and route calm.
BJM03.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: A time-of-day walking logic and quieter alternative are more useful than a famous-lane checklist.
BJM03.stop_condition: The guest has understood one public street pattern without entering private space.
BJM03.low_energy_branch: Use the shortest public lane sequence and finish at a calm public stop.
BJM03.rain_branch: Keep one covered/indoor neighbourhood layer and postpone a long lane walk.
BJM03.body_cost: Moderate walking with crossings, shade changes, crowds and privacy friction.

BJM04.guest_need: A visitor wants the Great Wall section that fits their body, scenery priority and time.
BJM04.hidden_need: Prevent fame or internet rankings from hiding transfer and return cost.
BJM04.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: The correct section is a trade-off decision, not a universal best-of list.
BJM04.stop_condition: The guest has a verified section, ascent/return plan and weather fallback.
BJM04.low_energy_branch: Choose the lower-load option or remove the Wall rather than forcing an endurance day.
BJM04.rain_branch: Do not release without current weather, surface, transport and access checks.
BJM04.body_cost: High transfer and variable step load; the return plan matters as much as the ascent.

BJM05.guest_need: A visitor wants water, gardens and imperial leisure as a different spatial experience.
BJM05.hidden_need: Decide whether the extra distance earns a place after the Palace Museum.
BJM05.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: It adds water, movement and landscape rather than another compact monument.
BJM05.stop_condition: The guest can articulate the contrast between ceremonial axis and imperial retreat.
BJM05.low_energy_branch: Choose the smaller central garden option or shorten the route.
BJM05.rain_branch: Keep only the confirmed indoor/covered layer and remove long lakeside movement.
BJM05.body_cost: Large-site walking and weather exposure create hidden fatigue.

BJM06.guest_need: A visitor wants contemporary Beijing through current cultural production, not a gallery crawl.
BJM06.hidden_need: Match the programme to the guest and protect against venue turnover.
BJM06.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: One exhibition-led district can answer a contemporary question better than multiple unconnected venues.
BJM06.stop_condition: The current programme has answered one art/design or industrial-reuse question.
BJM06.low_energy_branch: Choose one confirmed exhibition or public-facing district and stop.
BJM06.rain_branch: Useful indoor branch after programme, opening and ticket checks.
BJM06.body_cost: Lower physical intensity but high programme and transfer uncertainty.

BJM07.guest_need: A visitor needs the first 24 hours to work operationally.
BJM07.hidden_need: Prevent payment, identity, data or reservation friction from ruining the trip.
BJM07.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: A reliable arrival layer is more valuable than a famous attraction after a long flight.
BJM07.stop_condition: The guest can pay, navigate, access the next reservation and return safely.
BJM07.low_energy_branch: Keep the evening close to the hotel and defer the first major cultural anchor.
BJM07.rain_branch: Default arrival-day branch when outdoor plans are fragile.
BJM07.body_cost: Low sightseeing load, high jet-lag and operational sensitivity.

BJM08.guest_need: A visitor needs help deciding how many days Beijing deserves within a China journey.
BJM08.hidden_need: Protect against thin cross-city extensions and overpacked imperial days.
BJM08.why_this_over_nearby_alternative: A stay-length decision prevents another city from being added without a new question.
BJM08.stop_condition: The guest can name what an extra Beijing day adds and accept the transfer cost of any extension.
BJM08.low_energy_branch: Keep the coherent Beijing core rather than adding a thin extension.
BJM08.rain_branch: Use the strongest indoor contrast and current transport before changing cities.
BJM08.body_cost: Transfer fatigue and reservation order are the main costs.
